evidence: Start (What happened): Impact window opens at 05:55 UTC on 31 Jan 2023, when one partition in AZ-02 lost data access. | End (What happened): The impact window closes at 00:58 UTC on 1 Feb 2023. | Regions (What happened): Only East US 2 is named, with impact confined to physical zone AZ-02 and the other two zones unaffected.
notes: no publication date shown; the undated header 01/31/2023 matches the incident start date, so it is not coded as a publication date. Zone left empty: the report names only 'physical AZ-02', not a programmatic zone code. The response section says no failures were seen after 00:48 UTC on 1 Feb 2023 and the incident was then declared mitigated, which differs from the 00:58 window end used here. A second partition failed at about 11:43 UTC and VM creation in the zone was blocked from 12:04 UTC. Services: Virtual Machines (service management), Azure Backup, Azure Batch, Azure Data Factory, Azure Database for MySQL, Azure Database for PostgreSQL, Azure Databricks, Azure Kubernetes Service.

evidence: Start (What happened; What went wrong): Connectivity problems began at 07:08 UTC on 25 Jan 2023, when a router change in Madrid triggered recomputation. | End (What happened; How did we respond): Most regions and services were back by 09:05 UTC; residual packet loss lasted until full mitigation at 12:43 UTC. | Regions (title; What went wrong): The global WAN was affected across Azure regions; no specific region is named as the scope.
notes: no publication date shown; the undated header 01/25/2023 matches the incident date, so it is not coded as a publication date. Scope coded global from the title 'Global WAN issues' and the description of the Microsoft global network; no region codes are given. End uses the time most regions and services recovered (09:05 UTC); final networking equipment recovered 09:25 UTC and all issues were fully mitigated 12:43 UTC, with India and parts of North America recovering last. Madrid is named as the site of the change, not as an impacted region. Azure Government cloud services dependent on public cloud were also impacted. Services counted: Azure WAN networking connectivity, Microsoft 365, Power Platform, ExpressRoute, VPN Gateway, Virtual WAN.

evidence: Start (What happened): Latency and intermittent connectivity for some customers began at 15:39 UTC on 23 Jan 2023. | End (What happened; How did we respond): Impact window ends 19:38 UTC, when the faulty router was isolated and removed, mitigating the incident. | Regions (What happened; What went wrong): South Central US, through its Regional Network Gateway serving traffic between zones and in and out of the region.
notes: no publication date shown; the undated header 01/23/2023 matches the incident date, so it is not coded as a publication date. No zone named; the fault was in the regional gateway. Services counted: regional networking, Azure App Services, Azure Cosmos DB, Azure IoT Hub, Azure SQL DB.

evidence: Start (What happened; What went wrong): Ubuntu 18.04 VMs began receiving the faulty systemd update at 06:00 UTC on 30 Aug 2022. | End (What happened; How did we respond): The window closes 16:00 UTC on 31 Aug 2022, which the report later calls the final mitigation time. | Regions (What happened): Every Azure region was affected, including public and sovereign clouds.

evidence: Start (What happened; What went wrong): Access failures began at 02:47 UTC on 27 Aug 2022 with a regional utility power event. | End (What happened): Most customers were recovered by 07:00 UTC on 27 Aug; the final resources returned by 02:00 UTC on 28 Aug. | Regions (What went wrong): West US 2 lost utility power across all three zones; impact hit two datacenters in two different zones.
notes: no publication date shown; the undated header 08/27/2022 matches the incident start date, so it is not coded as a publication date. Scope regional: two datacenters in two different Availability Zones of West US 2 were impacted; the zones are not identified, so zones is empty. End uses the time most customers recovered (07:00 UTC on 27 Aug 2022); the last resources needing manual recovery returned by 02:00 UTC on 28 Aug 2022. Internal inconsistency: the response section says the Ultra Disk scale unit was not fully available until 21:40 UTC on 8/28, after the stated 02:00 UTC end. Power to all affected racks was restored by 04:46 UTC on 27 Aug. Services counted: Storage, Virtual Machines, App Services, Application Insights, Azure Database for PostgreSQL, Azure Red Hat OpenShift, Azure Search, Azure SQL DB, Backup, Data Explorer, ExpressRoute, NetApp Files.
